rules: When generating a path, output the shortest valid path under the implied connectivity.
Do not repeat a room in the path unless necessary.

variants.flat: You are in a building. You start at the Entrance (R1), located at (0,0), which contains a Cabinet and a Desk. Moving East from the Entrance (R1), you enter the Kitchen (R2) at (4,0), which contains a Cabinet and a Fridge. Moving West from the Kitchen (R2), you enter the Living Room (R3) at (0,4), which contains a Desk and a Wardrobe. Moving East from the Living Room (R3), you enter the Bedroom (R4) at (4,4), which contains a Bed and a Desk. Interestingly, the Bedroom features a connection back to the Entrance. At t1, a 'Master_Key' was in the Entrance (R1). At t2, it was picked up and moved to the Kitchen (R2). At t3, it was picked up and moved to the Living Room (R3).
variants.hier:
[SCENE: building]
- [ROOM R1: Entrance @ (0,0)]
  - [Objects: Appliance(Cabinet), Storage(Desk)]
- [ROOM R2: Kitchen @ (4,0)]
  - [Objects: Furniture(Cabinet), Appliance(Fridge)]
- [ROOM R3: Living Room @ (0,4)]
  - [Objects: Storage(Desk), Appliance(Wardrobe)]
- [ROOM R4: Bedroom @ (4,4)]
  - [Objects: Furniture(Bed), Appliance(Desk)]

[TOPOLOGY] R1-R2, R2-R3, R3-R4, R4-R1
[HISTORY] Master_Key: R1(t1) -> R2(t2) -> R3(t3)
variants.clustered:
[SCENE: building]
- [ZONE A: R1, R3]
  - [R1, R3 Objects]: {Appliance, Storage}
- [ZONE B: R2, R4]
  - [R2, R4 Objects]: {Furniture, Appliance}

[GEOMETRY] A_Center: (0.0, 2.0) | B_Center: (4.0, 2.0)
[CONNECTIVITY] Zone_A <-> Zone B via R1-R2. Zone_B <-> Zone A via R2-R3
[HISTORY] Master_Key: Zone_A(R1) -> Zone_A(R3)
